title: Reachable noise and existence of operator-valued Wishart processes
oneLine: Drift-reachable noise determines the candidate existence domain for operator-valued Wishart covariance processes.
abstract: This unrefereed candidate classifies continuous positive trace-class Wishart processes with deterministic initial covariance by the dimension reached by the noise under the adjoint semigroup, the initial rank outside that subspace, and continuity of a Gaussian convolution. It addresses the noninteger existence questions of Cox, Cuchiero and Khedher and isolates a precise operator-order issue in a printed sufficient condition. Established finite-dimensional results and Gaussian partition methods are explicitly credited.

narration: Where noise can reach. An Evidence Press audio briefing. Covariance describes how different quantities fluctuate together. Wishart processes model covariances that evolve randomly over time. In an infinite-dimensional model, however, writing down an equation does not guarantee that a suitable process exists. This candidate paper asks exactly which parameters and initial covariances are possible. Its key idea is to follow where the noise travels under the deterministic evolution. Noise entering through just one direction can eventually reach infinitely many directions. When that happens, the candidate classification forces the model parameter to be an integer, with a corresponding bound on the initial covariance rank. A separate continuity condition on a Gaussian process is also necessary. When the noise remains within a finite-dimensional subspace, the paper gives a different threshold, which also counts initial covariance outside that subspace. The argument combines established finite-dimensional Wishart results with a singular-scale reduction and explicit constructions. It also gives a counterexample to one precisely identified operator-order assumption in an earlier paper. This does not invalidate all of that paper's results. The proposed classification could help researchers check whether covariance models are mathematically admissible. It does not establish improved option pricing or empirical performance. The package contains a thirteen-page proof, exact finite checks and review responses. These checks do not certify the infinite-dimensional theorem. This is an unrefereed candidate dated September twenty-second, twenty twenty-six. The full paper and evidence are linked on the release page. This is an AI-generated voice summary, not additional evidence.
